chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Yahya ibn Zakariyya, from his father Zakariyya ibn Musa, from al-Qasim ibn Ubayd Allah al-Qummi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who prays over a funeral alone. He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And two men pray over it?' He said, 'Yes, but the other stands behind the other, and he does not stand by his side.'
ai.seo_question: How should two people stand when praying over a funeral together according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the spatial arrangement of the Imam in Janazah prayer, distinguishing between solitary and paired performance. It establishes that while a single individual may lead the prayer independently, two individuals must stand in a single file (one behind the other) rather than side-by-side, reflecting the Shia juristic preference for maintaining the singular leadership structure even in small groups.
